strings.remote.title: Remote Access
strings.remote.intro: Let other people control this manager from their own device with a short code. Share the whole app or a single world, choose exactly which tabs they can use, and revoke access any time.
strings.remote.enableDesc: Turn on to let people join with a code. While off, the manager is reachable only from this computer.
strings.remote.lanDesc: Open the manager to other devices on your network. Applying this restarts the local server.
strings.remote.lanDescWeb: Bind the manager to your network so other devices can reach it. Restart the app to apply.
strings.remote.lanOffHint: Turn on same-network access above to get a link others on your network can open.
strings.remote.tunnelHint: Using a tunnel (playit.gg, Cloudflare Tunnel, ngrok)? Point it at this computer's port and share the tunnel's /remote URL — cross-origin requests are handled.
strings.remote.noCodes: No codes yet. Create one to share access.
strings.remote.scopeFullDesc: Access to every world, limited to the tabs you allow.
strings.remote.scopeWorldDesc: Access to a single world only.
strings.remote.deleteConfirm: Delete code {{code}}? Anyone using it loses access immediately. Its activity log is kept.
strings.remote.tabsHelp: The Admin tab (ports, passwords, install folder) is off by default. Enable it only for people you fully trust.
strings.remote.pickWorld: Pick a world for a per-world code.
strings.remote.entryHelp: Type the 5-digit code the server owner shared with you.
strings.remote.lockedOut: Too many attempts. Try again shortly.

strings.info.guideBotSubtitle: Make your own Discord bot so your group can start, stop and back up the server without this app
strings.info.whatIsBotDesc: A Discord bot you own, that adds /start, /stop, /restart, /broadcast and /backup to your Discord server. You make it in a couple of minutes, and it only ever talks to your copy of this app — nothing goes through anyone else's servers.
strings.info.bot1: Open the developer portal and click New Application (top right). Give it the name you want people to see in Discord — your server's name works well — agree to the terms and click Create.
strings.info.bot2: On the General Information page you can add an icon and description. This is what your group sees when they click the bot, so it's worth a minute.
strings.info.bot3: Click Bot in the left sidebar. This is where the bot's identity lives. You do not need to switch on any of the Privileged Gateway Intents — this app never reads messages or member lists, so leave them all off.
strings.info.bot4: On the Bot page click Reset Token, confirm, and copy the long string it shows you. This is shown only once — if you lose it, reset it again and copy the new one. Treat it like a password: anyone with it controls the bot.
strings.info.bot5: Go to your world → the Discord Bot tab, paste the token and save. The app checks it with Discord and then shows an invite link. Open it, pick your Discord server, and confirm — it asks for no permissions.
strings.info.bot6Title: Link it and pick who can use it
strings.info.bot6: In Discord, run /authorize. It opens a private box asking for the world's admin password (the world's Admin tab in this app) — nobody else can see what you type. After that, come back to the Discord Bot tab and choose the roles or people allowed to run the commands. Until you do, only you can.
strings.info.bot7Title: Optional: pick people from a list
strings.info.bot7: By default the app can list your server's roles, but not its people — Discord hides that unless you allow it. If you'd rather tick names off a list than paste IDs, go back to the portal → your app → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents and turn on Server Members Intent, then press Refresh on the Discord Bot tab. It only lets the app read who's in the server; it still can't read any messages. Skip it if you prefer — adding people by ID works either way.
strings.info.botSafety: The token never leaves your computer and is never shown again once saved. The bot is invited with no permissions at all — it can't read your messages or post on its own, only answer these commands. Only the roles and people you pick can use them, and everyone else is refused. If the token ever leaks, hit Reset Token in the portal and paste the new one here — the old one dies instantly.
strings.bot.step1Desc: Make your own Discord bot and paste its token here — it stays on this computer and is never shown again. <guide>Step-by-step guide</guide>.
strings.bot.tokenPlaceholder: Bot token from the Discord developer portal
strings.bot.tokenReplace: Paste a new token to replace this one
strings.bot.tokenSaved: Bot token saved — the bot is connecting.
strings.bot.confirmRemove: Remove this bot? The token is deleted and the Discord commands stop working.
strings.bot.step2Title: 2. Invite it to your Discord server
strings.bot.step2Desc: This link asks for no permissions at all — the bot only answers the commands below. You need Manage Server on the Discord side to add it.
strings.bot.notInAnyServer: The bot is online but isn't in any Discord server yet — open the link below and add it. The commands only exist inside a server.
strings.bot.step3Desc: In your Discord server, run /authorize. It opens a private box asking for this world's admin password (the world's Admin tab). Nobody else in the channel sees what you type. This page updates itself once it's done.
strings.bot.notifyChannelDesc: Where the bot posts the one-minute warning before an idle world is auto-stopped, when no webhook is set up for it. The bot must be able to send messages in the channel you pick.
strings.bot.statusBoardDesc: Pin a status card to a channel and the bot keeps that one message updated — online/offline, in-game day, player count and who's on — instead of posting a new /status every time. Pick a channel and send; add more for other channels or servers.
strings.bot.statusBoardSent: Status card posted — it'll stay updated
strings.bot.statusBoardHint: The bot must be able to Send Messages and Embed Links in the channel. Deleting the message in Discord stops that card automatically. Which fields show follows the /status settings above.
strings.bot.step4Desc: Only the roles and people you pick here can run the commands. Everyone else is refused, even in the same channel.
strings.bot.noRoles: No roles found. Roles created by other bots are hidden, since they can't be given to a person — and @everyone is left out on purpose, because it would mean the whole server.
strings.bot.listRefreshed: Roles and people re-loaded from Discord.
strings.bot.needIntentTitle: Turn on one switch to pick people from a list
strings.bot.needIntentDesc: Discord won't tell an app who's in a server unless its Server Members Intent is on. Turn it on in the developer portal → your app → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents, then hit Refresh. Show me how. It's optional — you can always add someone by ID below.
strings.bot.userIdHint: To copy an ID: Discord → Settings → Advanced → turn on Developer Mode, then right-click someone → Copy User ID.
strings.bot.badUserId: That doesn't look like a Discord user ID — it should be a long number.
strings.bot.nobodyWarn: No roles or people are picked, so nobody can use the commands right now.
strings.bot.whoCanWhatDesc: Adding someone gives them everything — untick anything they shouldn't have. Someone with no ticks left is refused entirely.
strings.bot.statusFieldsDesc: This card goes to the whole channel, not just whoever asked.
strings.bot.statusAddressHint: Server name and address come from Settings → Server Identity. The address only appears once you've set a Public IP there — blank means the server works its own out, which this app can't see.
strings.bot.logDesc: Every command anyone has run from Discord, including the ones that were refused.

strings.bot.cmdBroadcast: show a message to everyone playing
strings.bot.cmdKick: remove someone who's playing — pick them from a list of who's online
strings.bot.appMustRun: These only work while RSDW Sync is open — the bot listens from this app.
strings.world.noLan: No LAN address detected — the server still listens on all network adapters; use this PC's IP from your OS network settings.
strings.world.connectHelp: In RuneScape Dragonwilds: Join Multiplayer → Connect via IP and paste an address above. Players on your network use the LAN address; from this same PC use 127.0.0.1. The server isn't bound to any one address — it listens on every adapter on port {{port}}. For friends over the internet, forward/tunnel UDP port {{port}} and share your public IP.
strings.world.playitLink: → Want friends to join over the internet? See the free playit.gg guide
strings.world.deleteIntro: Choose what to remove. This cannot be undone.
strings.world.deleteProfileOnlyDesc: Removes this world from the manager. Server files, saves, and mods on disk are kept — you can re-add the folder later.
strings.world.deleteWithFiles: Delete profile + server files on disk
strings.world.deleteWithFilesDesc: Permanently deletes the entire install folder ({{dir}}) including all saves and backups. There is no recovery.

strings.map.calSaved: Saved — this calibration only affects your install
strings.map.calSavedGlobal: Global calibration saved — it ships with the app

strings.map.calNoPlayers: No players online — bring one online to calibrate.
strings.mapCal.title: Map calibration (developer)
strings.mapCal.intro: Connect to a running Palworld server's REST API, then place reference points to solve where world coordinates land on the map image. Saving writes public/map/calibration.json, which ships with the app — so end users never have to calibrate.
strings.mapCal.restHint: The server's REST API must be enabled. The default REST port is 8212.
strings.mapCal.noPlayers: Connected, but no players are online. Bring a player online to place reference points.
strings.mapCal.howto: Click Calibrate, pick a player, then zoom in and click their exact spot. Do 3+ spread-out spots (e.g. start, desert, Feybreak), then Save.
strings.create.addIntro: Install a fresh Runescape Dragonwilds dedicated server, or register a server you already have on disk.
strings.create.installNewDesc: Download the dedicated server with SteamCMD into a folder you choose.
strings.create.useExistingDesc: Point to a Dragonwilds server folder you already downloaded. No re-download.
strings.create.installFolderHint: SteamCMD installs the dedicated server (app 4019830) here. Each world needs its own folder.
strings.create.targetPlatformHint: Only choose a platform other than this machine's if you plan to move the files to that platform afterward — this app can't run a Windows server on Linux (or vice versa) without Wine.
strings.create.browsePlaceholder: Click Browse to choose a folder
strings.create.typePathToast: Type the full server folder path (native picker is in the desktop app).
strings.create.installStarted: Install started — track progress in the downloads tray
strings.create.adminPasswordHint: Leave blank to auto-generate. Used for REST API + RCON auth.
strings.create.serverFolderLabel: Server folder or Dragonwilds server path
strings.create.serverFolderHint: Point to the folder containing the server binary (Windows) or the server start script (Linux).
strings.create.browseFolderPlaceholder: Click Browse to choose the folder
strings.create.osWarning: ⚠ This build targets a different OS than this machine.
strings.create.keepPassword: Keep the server's existing admin password (from its settings file)
strings.admin.serverPassword: Server password (players must enter to join)
strings.admin.serverPasswordPlaceholder: Leave blank for an open server (anyone can join)
strings.admin.serverPasswordHint: This is the in-game join password (Palworld's ServerPassword), separate from the admin password. Blank = open server. Restart the world to apply.
strings.admin.communityDesc: Lists this world in Palworld's in-game public server browser so anyone can find and join it. Off means private — friends join by IP only. Adds the -publiclobby launch flag.
strings.admin.communityNote: Note: to actually appear in the list, the server must be reachable from the internet (port-forwarded or tunneled). Restart the world after changing this.
strings.admin.legacyPerfDesc: Passes -useperfthreads, -NoAsyncLoadingThread, and -UseMultithreadForDS at launch. Palworld's engine has handled multithreading on its own since 1.0, so some servers now run better with these left off. On by default to match every earlier version of this app — nothing changes unless you turn it off.
strings.admin.legacyPerfNote: Keep this on if you run PalDefender or another anti-cheat — it needs -NoAsyncLoadingThread to avoid heap-corruption crashes. Takes effect the next time this world starts.
strings.admin.rconDesc: Writes RCONEnabled=True and the RCON port to DedicatedServer.ini so tools that still rely on RCON can connect. Off by default — this manager itself uses the REST API for everything and rewrites this setting on each start, so leave it on to stop your RCONEnabled=true from being reset.
strings.admin.rconNote: Pocketpair has deprecated RCON and plans to remove it, but it still works today. Takes effect the next time this world starts.
strings.admin.crashRestarted_one: Crash guardian has restarted this world {{count}} time.
strings.admin.crashRestarted_other: Crash guardian has restarted this world {{count}} times.
strings.admin.installFolderDesc: Where this world's server files live. The Mods, saves, and settings are all read from here, so point this at the correct RSDragonwilds folder (on any drive). The world must be stopped to change it.
strings.admin.stopToChangeFolder: Stop the world to change its folder.
strings.admin.stopBeforeFolder: Stop the world before changing its install folder.
strings.admin.portsHint: Only the game UDP port needs to be reachable by players (port-forward this one on your router). Keep the REST API port LAN-only. RCON is deprecated by Pocketpair and disabled by default — this manager uses the REST API for all administration.
strings.admin.portsHintStop: Stop the world to change ports.
strings.admin.portsHintNext: Changes take effect the next time this world starts.
strings.admin.stopBeforePorts: Stop the world before changing its ports.
strings.admin.portsUpdated: Ports updated — start the world to apply
strings.admin.envVarsHint: One KEY=value per line. Applied to the server process on launch; also lets you override the Wine defaults below (e.g. WINEDEBUG).
strings.admin.wineDesc: This world runs Windows binaries. On a Linux host it launches automatically through Wine using these settings; a native Windows host ignores them.
strings.admin.winePrefixPlaceholder: Leave blank for an auto-managed prefix
strings.admin.stopBeforeWine: Stop the world before changing Wine settings.
strings.admin.wineLaunchFlagsHint: Passed to the wine command itself, before the server executable — not the same as the launch arguments above, which go to the server.

strings.backups.importPickerDesktop: Save import via file picker is available in the desktop app.

strings.broadcast.modCopiedNoUe4ss: Broadcast mod copied, but UE4SS was not detected — install UE4SS first.
strings.broadcast.confirmRemoveMod: Remove the on-screen broadcast mod? Broadcasts fall back to the chat-feed announce until you reinstall it. Restart the world to fully unload the mod.
strings.broadcast.modRemoved: Broadcast mod removed. Restart the world to unload it.
strings.broadcast.pickFuture: Pick a time in the future
strings.broadcast.wantOnScreenDesc: Broadcast-to-players is not supported in this app for Dragonwilds.
strings.broadcast.stopToChangeMod: Stop the world to change the broadcast mod.
strings.broadcast.enableDesc: UE4SS is installed. Add the bundled broadcast mod to show messages on every player's screen, then restart the world to load it. Until then, broadcasts appear in the chat feed.
strings.broadcast.stopToInstall: Stop the world to install the broadcast mod.
strings.broadcast.modOnRest: — messages show as the on-screen server notice while the world runs.
strings.broadcast.stopToRemoveMod: Stop the world to remove the broadcast mod
strings.broadcast.noneScheduled: No scheduled broadcasts. They fire once at the set time, then disappear. If the app is closed past the time, the broadcast is kept and flagged as missed.
strings.broadcast.missedLine: Missed — was due {{time}}. Reschedule it or send it now.
strings.broadcast.footerModOn: Broadcasts show on-screen via the installed mod (the server's on-screen notice). The red pre-shutdown countdown look is exclusive to actual shutdowns and can't be triggered for a normal message.
strings.broadcast.footerModOff: Broadcast-to-players is not supported in this app for Dragonwilds.
strings.info.title: Info & Guides
strings.info.subtitle: Optional help for getting the most out of your server.
strings.info.guideInternetTitle: How to host your server on the internet
strings.info.guideInternetSubtitle: Make your world joinable by friends anywhere — free, no port forwarding
strings.info.whatIsPlayitDesc: A free tunneling service that gives your local server a public address, so friends can join over the internet without port forwarding or router changes. This is a recommendation, not a requirement — if you already have port forwarding set up, you don't need it.
strings.info.step1: Go to playit.gg, create a free account, and download the playit agent for Windows.
strings.info.step2: Run the downloaded agent and sign in / link it to your account when the browser opens. Leave it running.
strings.info.step3: In the playit.gg dashboard, add a new tunnel.
strings.info.step4: Palworld uses UDP. Choose the UDP tunnel type on the free tier.
strings.info.step5: You only need a single port for one world, so set the port allocation to 1.
strings.info.step6Intro: Point the tunnel at your machine:
strings.info.step6LocalPort: Local port: your world's game port (e.g. 8211 — shown on the world page)
strings.info.step7: playit.gg gives you a public IP and port. Share that with friends — in Palworld they use Join Multiplayer → Connect via IP and paste it. Done!
strings.settings.title: Settings
strings.settings.cat.gameDesc: Creature name overrides and in-game chat capture.
strings.settings.cat.updatesDesc: Automatic Dragonwilds server updates and how often to check.
strings.settings.cat.backupsDesc: How many to keep and where they're stored.
strings.settings.cat.desktopDesc: Launch on startup, tray behaviour and the server console window.
strings.settings.chatCaptureDesc: Capture in-game chat via the UE4SS relay mod. Turn this off to stop the app from reading chat entirely. If a Palworld update ever makes the mod misbehave, also use Remove chat mod on each world's Chat tab to take the mod off the server.
strings.settings.autoLaunchDesc: Launch the app when you log in to Windows or Linux, so your servers can be brought back up without opening it yourself. On by default — turn this off if you'd rather start it manually. When it starts at login it opens straight to the system tray; open it from the tray icon (which also lists your worlds).
strings.settings.closeToTrayDesc: When on (the default), the window's close button hides the app to the system tray and your servers keep running in the background. Open it again from the tray icon, or quit for real from the tray menu. Turn this off to make the close button quit the app.
strings.settings.hideConsoleDesc: Start Dragonwilds servers without an extra console window. Server output remains available from the Logs tab, and managed shutdown still works normally.
strings.settings.hideConsoleWarn: The console window is showing. It's the only place Palworld's raw server output appears, so leave this off if you read it. Turn it on to start servers without it.
strings.settings.autoUpdateDesc: Off by default. When on, any server running an out-of-date Dragonwilds build is updated automatically: players are warned in-game, the server is stopped once, a safety backup is taken, SteamCMD updates it, and the same profile is brought back up. The app itself is never auto-updated — new app versions are only shown.
strings.settings.updateCheckIntervalHelp: How often to check Steam for a new Dragonwilds dedicated-server build. Minimum 5 minutes. This check keeps the update badge accurate whether or not automatic updates are on.
strings.settings.keepLastN: Keep last N backups per world
strings.settings.backupLocationDesc: Backups are ZIP snapshots of each world's Saved folder, stored outside the server so a game update can't touch them. Currently saving to {{where}}:
strings.settings.backupPathPlaceholder: Leave blank for the default location
strings.settings.existingBackupsNote: Existing backups stay where they are — only new backups go to the new folder.
strings.settings.steamcmdNote: — installed automatically on first world provisioning.
strings.settings.devDesc: Advanced tools for building and customizing the app.
strings.settings.devCalibrateDesc: Connect to a Palworld REST API, place reference points, and bake the map calibration into the app so every install gets accurate dots.
strings.common.pickerDesktop: File picker is available in the desktop app.
strings.common.folderPickerDesktop: Folder picker is available in the desktop app.
strings.players.name: Name
strings.players.activityDesc: Everyone who has joined this world, ranked by login streak. Built from stored join history — no setup needed.
strings.players.noHistory: No login history yet — it fills in as players join.
strings.players.modStreakTip: Streak from the DailyLoginRewards mod, kept in sync with what it awards.
strings.players.modConfigHelp: The app auto-detects the DailyLoginRewards players.json under this world's UE4SS Mods folder. Set a path manually, or upload the file if the server is on another machine.
strings.players.modUploaded_one: Imported {{count}} streak from the uploaded file.
strings.players.modUploaded_other: Imported {{count}} streaks from the uploaded file.
strings.chat.stopBeforeChange: Stop the world before changing the chat mod.
strings.chat.installedRestart: Chat mod installed. Restart the world to start capturing chat.
strings.chat.copiedNoUe4ss: Chat mod copied, but UE4SS was not detected — install UE4SS first.
strings.chat.confirmRemove: Remove the chat relay mod from this server? Chat capture stops until you reinstall it. Restart the world to fully unload the mod.
strings.chat.removedRestart: Chat relay mod removed. Restart the world to unload it.
strings.chat.captureOffDesc: The in-game chat capture feature is disabled globally. Turn it back on in <s>Settings</s> to read chat again.
strings.chat.needsUe4ssDesc: In-game chat is captured by a small UE4SS Lua mod. UE4SS (the Lua mod loader) isn’t installed on this world yet — install it first, then come back and add the chat relay mod.
strings.chat.stopToChange: Stop the world to change the chat mod.
strings.chat.installRelayDesc: UE4SS is installed. Add the bundled chat relay mod, then restart the world to start capturing chat.
strings.chat.stopToInstall: Stop the world to install the chat mod.
strings.chat.modInstalledRest: — player messages appear here live while the world runs.
strings.chat.stopToRemove: Stop the world to remove the chat mod
strings.chat.empty: No chat yet. In-game player messages appear here live while the world is running.
strings.chat.startToCapture: Start the world to capture chat.
strings.chat.announcePlaceholder: Broadcast an announcement to all players…
strings.chat.footer: Palworld has no REST endpoint to send as a player, so admin messages go out as a server announcement (broadcast to everyone).
strings.deaths.needsUe4ssDesc: Player deaths are read from the game by a small UE4SS mod. Install UE4SS first, then add the death relay mod.
strings.deaths.stopToChange: Stop the world to change the death mod.
strings.deaths.installRelayDesc: UE4SS is installed. Add the bundled death relay mod, then restart the world to start tracking deaths.
strings.deaths.stopToInstall: Stop the world to install the death mod.
strings.deaths.installedRestart: Death mod installed — restart the world to activate it.
strings.deaths.copiedNoUe4ss: Copied, but UE4SS wasn't detected — install UE4SS for it to load.
strings.deaths.modInstalledRest: — deaths appear here and in the Overview log while the world runs.
strings.deaths.stopToRemove: Stop the world to remove the death mod
strings.deaths.confirmRemove: Remove the death tracking mod from this world?
strings.deaths.removedRestart: Death mod removed — restart the world to apply.
strings.deaths.emptyNeedsMod: Install the death relay mod above to start tracking deaths.
strings.palmap.globalDesc: Rename how creatures appear in death messages everywhere. These apply to every world; a world can override any of them in its Deaths tab. Unnamed creatures seen in-game show up at the top.
strings.palmap.worldDesc: Override display names just for this world. Left blank, a name inherits the global setting, then the built-in default. Newly-seen creatures on this world appear at the top.
strings.palmap.hint: Placeholder text shows the name a blank field inherits. Clearing a box reverts it.
strings.schedule.playerFilterHint: The name box picks whose join fires this — leave it blank to fire for anyone.
strings.schedule.joinDelayTip: Seconds to wait after the join before sending. 0 sends right away.
strings.schedule.joinDelayHint: The delay waits that many seconds after they join before sending — a few seconds gives them time to finish loading in.
strings.schedule.httpHint: Sends an HTTP request to your own API/integration on this schedule — handy for triggering custom commands across servers without doing it by hand. Headers are one "Name: value" per line; the body is sent as-is (set a Content-Type header if it's JSON).
strings.schedule.systemHint: Sent as a System announcement in the in-game chat feed.
strings.schedule.onscreenHint: Shown on players' screens (needs the on-screen notice mod; falls back to chat).
strings.schedule.playerTokenHint: Use {player} to insert the player's name.
strings.schedule.onscreenNeedsModTitle: On-screen notices need the broadcast mod
strings.schedule.onscreenNeedsModDesc: This world doesn't have the on-screen broadcast mod set up yet, so scheduled notices will fall back to the chat feed. Set it up on the Broadcast tab to show them on players' screens.
strings.schedule.empty: No scheduled jobs. Add automatic restarts, backups, updates, or timed messages on a maintenance window.
strings.schedule.skipNextTip: Skip only the next occurrence — the schedule stays on and resumes afterward.
strings.schedule.idleHint: Stops this world once nobody has been online for the set time. A player joining resets the timer. If a Discord webhook or bot is set up, players get a one-minute warning first (webhook preferred); otherwise it just shuts down. Needs the REST API so it can see who's online.
strings.warn.title: Warn players before restart / update / scheduled stop
strings.warn.desc: Broadcasts a countdown in-game before a restart or update, and before a scheduled stop, then hands off to Palworld's native red shutdown countdown for the final minute. The manual Stop button and Force-stop go down promptly without the countdown. Requires the REST API (on by default).
strings.warn.hint: Set Repeat every to 0 (or ≥ the start time) to warn just once. Example: start 10, repeat 2 → notices at 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 minutes, then the red countdown.
strings.warn.defaultMessage: The server will restart in {minutes} minute(s). Please get to a safe place.
strings.mods.confirmRemove: Remove mod "{{pkg}}"? Its files will be deleted.
strings.mods.windowsOnly: Palworld server-side mods run on the Windows dedicated server only. This host isn't Windows, so mods may not load even if configured here.
strings.mods.runningNotice: The world is running. Stop it to add, enable/disable, or remove mods — these changes only take effect at boot.
strings.mods.bootNotice: Mods load only when the server starts — restart the world after making changes. On restart, the game deploys each active mod according to its Info.json.
strings.mods.globalEnabled: Enabled — active mods will load on next start.
strings.mods.workshopPlaceholder: Steam Workshop ID (already downloaded in Steam)
strings.mods.workshopHelpAria: How to find a Workshop ID
strings.mods.noSteamDetected: No Dragonwilds install was auto-detected. Select the game's main Steam folder, or any folder inside RSDragonwilds.
strings.mods.noGameModsDetected: No PAK, UE4SS, RuneSchema, or supported binary mods were found in this installation.
strings.mods.syncSelectionSaved: Retained mod selection synchronized to this World
strings.mods.empty: No mods installed. Import a Workshop-style mod (.zip containing Info.json), or add one you've subscribed to in Steam by its Workshop ID.
strings.mods.danglingNotice: These mods are listed as active but their files aren't on disk: {{list}}. Re-import them or disable them.
strings.mods.wsModalIntro: PSM adds a Workshop mod from the copy Steam has already downloaded on this PC — it doesn't download it for you. So the order is: subscribe in Steam first, then add it here by its ID.
strings.mods.wsStep1: Subscribe in Steam. Open the mod on the Palworld Steam Workshop and click Subscribe. Steam downloads it into your Steam library's workshop folder.
strings.mods.wsStep2: Copy its Workshop ID. It's the number at the end of the mod's URL — steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1234567890. The number is the ID.
strings.mods.wsStep3: Paste the ID into the field and click Add. PSM finds it across your Steam libraries (any drive) and installs it into this world.
strings.mods.wsModalNote: No Steam copy? Use Import mod (.zip) instead — pick a mod archive that contains an Info.json and PSM will install it directly, no subscription needed.
strings.mods.updatesNeverChecked: Not checked yet — compare your copies against Steam's.
strings.mods.updatesPending_one: {{count}} mod has a newer version on Steam.
strings.mods.updatesPending_other: {{count}} mods have newer versions on Steam.
strings.mods.updatesAllCurrent: Every mod matches the version Steam has.
strings.mods.openFolderDesktop: Opening folders only works in the desktop app.
strings.mods.updatesNone: All mods are up to date.
strings.mods.modUpdated: Updated {{name}} from v{{from}} to v{{to}} — restart to apply.
strings.mods.notServerModTip: This mod's Info.json has no InstallRule with IsServer, so Palworld won't deploy it on a dedicated server on its own.
strings.mods.forceEnableTip: Not marked as a server mod — enabling asks you to confirm first.
strings.mods.forceIntro: This mod's Info.json never declares IsServer, so Palworld's own mod deployment skips it. Plenty of mods run on a server anyway — the author just didn't write server install rules.
strings.mods.forceLua: This one ships Lua scripts, which PSM copies into UE4SS itself — so forcing it should work. Restart the world to apply.
strings.mods.forcePakOnly: This one is Pak-only, and only Palworld's own deploy step can install those — forcing it may do nothing. Enable it, restart, and check the console.
strings.discord.testSent: Test message sent — check your Discord channel
strings.discord.notificationsDesc: Add one or more Discord webhook channels for this world, then choose which channel each event posts to below — e.g. a Status channel for start/stop/crash, a separate Backup channel, and a Chat channel for the in-game relay.
strings.discord.noChannels: No channels yet. Add one to start posting notifications.
strings.discord.routeDesc: Pick the channel each event posts to, or Don't send to mute it.
strings.discord.chatNeedsMod: Needs the chat relay mod installed on the Chat tab.
strings.discord.channelNoUrl: This channel has no webhook URL — nothing will be sent.
strings.discord.templatesDesc: Customize the text posted for each event. Leave one blank to use the built-in default. Click a placeholder to insert it — they're filled in when the message is sent.
strings.discord.relayDesc: Post this world's captured in-game chat to the webhook above for a Palworld→Discord feed. Needs the chat relay mod installed on the Chat tab.
strings.ue4ss.stopBeforeInstall: Stop the world before installing UE4SS.

strings.ue4ss.title: UE4SS / Lua mods
strings.ue4ss.desc: UE4SS runs Lua script mods (the kind commonly published on Nexus). This is separate from the Steam Workshop system above. Mods install under your server's UE4SS mods folder (<install>\Binaries\Win64\ue4ss\Mods on UE4SS 3.0).
strings.ue4ss.notInstalledTitle: UE4SS isn’t installed for this world
strings.ue4ss.notInstalledDesc: Download the UE4SS release zip (the dedicated-server build) from its official page, then install it here. The app extracts it into Win64 and sets the dedicated-server-safe options for you.
strings.ue4ss.consoleEnabledDesc: GuiConsoleVisible is on, which crashes a dedicated server on launch. Turn it off.
strings.ue4ss.stopToManage: Stop the world to add, enable/disable, or remove Lua mods.
strings.ue4ss.loadsAtBoot: UE4SS only loads mods at server boot.
strings.ue4ss.emptyMods: No UE4SS mods yet. Import a Lua mod (.zip containing Scripts/main.lua).
strings.ue4ss.restartNote: Mods load at server boot — restart the world after making changes.

strings.prereqs.title: Missing Windows runtimes
strings.prereqs.desc: This server needs {{missing}} to run. Without it Palworld exits immediately at startup. Install the prerequisites, then start the world.

strings.prereqs.manualVc: Or download Visual C++ from Microsoft
